title: GRAPHLCP: Structure-Aware Localized Conformal Prediction on Graphs
claim: A frozen model's embeddings pass through four sequential stages (transform, densify, propagate, calibrate) to yield localized uncertainty estimates.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, numbered circles 1-4 on arrows, frozen-model box on top
description: A wide single-row pipeline diagram. At top left an input graph, shown as a small node-link graph with nodes A–G in salmon and a feature-matrix heatmap, feeds via an arrow into a dotted gray box titled 'GNN Model (Frozen)'. The box holds a 'Message-Passing Encoding' block and a 'Linear Classifier' block joined by a dashed arrow labeled 'GNN Embeddings'. A dark-red line carries the embeddings down and left to an embedding heatmap. Dark-red arrows with numbered circles 1–4 then run along the bottom. Step 1 is a PCA plot with an elliptical Gaussian kernel, axes PC1/PC2, sqrt(lambda) markers, similarity values and tau_d = 0.5. Step 2 is the densified graph with new edges. Step 3 is the graph with nodes shaded by PPR influence and a colorbar. Step 4 is an upward arrow to a circled 4 beside the classifier output. Dark red is used consistently for the data flow.
caption: \ourmethod. Given the embeddings of a frozen GNN for an input graph, \ourmethod goes through four stages: 1) PCA Transformation: high-dimensional embeddings are decorrelated and largest eigenvalues (corresponding to directions of highest variance) yield an adaptive bandwidth for an anisotropic Gaussian kernel; 2) Graph Densification: adding informative edges using a fixed similarity threshold; 3) PPR Integration: utilizing the PPR kernel to sample anchor nodes (for each test sample) and weight calibration samples; and 4) Conformal Prediction: a weighted quantile is computed from calibration samples to construct the final prediction set/interval.
abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) provides a distribution-free approach to uncertainty quantification with finite-sample guarantees. However, applying CP to graph neural networks (GNNs) remains challenging as the combinatorial nature of graphs often leads to insufficiently certain predictions and indiscriminative embeddings. Existing methods primarily rely on embedding-space proximity for localization, which can be unreliable for graphs and yield uneven coverage across different graph regions. We propose GRAPHLCP, a proximity-based localized CP framework that incorporates graph topology and inter-node dependencies into localization and weighting. Our approach introduces a feature-aware densification step to mitigate locality bias in sparse graphs, followed by a Personalized PageRank-based kernel computation to model structural proximity. This enables topology-dependent anchor sampling and calibration weighting that captures both local and long-range dependencies. Extensive experiments on regression and classification datasets demonstrate that GRAPHLCP improves test-conditional coverage without excessive conservativeness, while preserving finite-sample marginal coverage.
